findings.observed_behavior: Pruning only works when agent-system/runtime and its resolved path are lexically identical. That holds in the normal layout and in the tests.
findings.reproducible_evidence: The pruning check compares the unresolved `Path(dirpath) / name` (built from os.walk(agent_system_root)) against `(agent_system_root / 'runtime').resolve()`. self.root is resolved, but if `agent-system` itself is a symlink, or any path component below root resolves differently, resolve() returns the target path. The two paths then never compare equal, so runtime/ is not pruned and its contracts are walked, read, and can be returned when they sort first.
findings.required_behavior: Prune runtime/ no matter how the agent-system path resolves. For example, compare against the unresolved `agent_system_root / 'runtime'`, or prune `name == 'runtime'` when `dirpath == agent_system_root`.
findings.required_outcome: Make the comparison path-consistent. This is a robustness improvement and does not block this change.
findings.violated_criterion: Discovery does not list or open files under agent-system/runtime/ (prune the directory while walking)

findings.observed_behavior: The test proves runtime files are not opened. It does not prove runtime/ is never traversed.
findings.reproducible_evidence: The test spies only on Path.read_text. An implementation that fully walks or lists runtime/ and filters the paths before reading would still pass, so the 'does not list ... before filtering' requirement has no test coverage.
findings.required_behavior: Optionally also show that runtime/ is never descended into. For example, spy on os.walk output, or put an unreadable directory under runtime/ and check that walking never reaches it.
findings.required_outcome: Add stronger regression protection for the pruning requirement. The implementation itself already prunes correctly via dirnames[:].
findings.violated_criterion: Tests exercise the real behavior (directory pruning, not just read filtering)
